notes.title: DEV BLOG #8
notes.content:
Hello again, its been a while. While the continued development cycle on Wild Europe is still uncertain, I thought I would touch up on what things I'm planning on doing later on. Firstly, I'm planning on doing other forms of content in the form of Books and (possibly) Boardgames! I also by no means have given up on game development. I feel that I overworked myself during the creation of Jacob Larkin's Wild Europe, and after a long time away I started to lose some interest in the project. I hope that this explains some of the lack of communication and updates. Finalizing Wild Europe's development early has indeed crossed my mind, and I will be sure to keep everyone up to date on this.

Until next time, and have a blessed day.

notes.title: DEV BLOG #7
notes.content:
Hi all, Its been AGES since my last post. To cut to the chase, I'm working on the creative process of making a new game. This time around there will hopefully be more work going into the marketing aspect.
For those concerned about the game's development, I'm planning on wrapping up development on Wild Europe by the end of the year. I initially promised myself to develop the game for at least a few years, but due to various factors I've managed to come to this decision (after all I am a solo developer with minimal resources at my disposal). Future titles are likely to be singleplayer only (but multiplayer titles are still under consideration).

Until next time, and have a blessed week ahead.

notes.title: New stuff on the way!/Dev Blog #6
notes.content:
Long story short I had taken a breather from Wild Europe and I'm now looking into making new games. Don't worry though, wild Europe will still be in development! In the time I've been away I have discovered a wealth of info on how to create flying/swimming AI, so you can expect flocks of birds and schools of fish coming soon!

In other news, if you didn't know already I am a huge dinosaur/prehistory geek. so future titles might include a blast from the past!

notes.title: DEV BLOG #5
notes.content:
Hello friends!

In today's developer blog I'd like to tell you that there is a major patch in the works.
While it does not yet have a name, it includes a new map!

The new map is a massive marshland with rivers and forests. Within its lands you will find a huge amount of new species to encounter and play with.

The game has also been going through various bug fixes and improvements regarding the water physics and carcass physics. Animals now float to the surface in deep water; furthermore, carcasses now fall to the ground upon an animal's death. while these might not sound like much, they are major steps towards improving the game's realism. 

I have also been hard at work at ironing out bugs and issues with the code (its a never ending struggle).


In other news: I've been not only juggling work on the game, but also in taking care of a new puppy at home!

Until next time, God bless and have a wonderful day!

notes.title: DEV BLOG #4
notes.content:
Today I'd like to chat about what is in the works for update 1.2.2
it won't feature new species but it will come with a wealth of new features.

New feature 1: AI birds
The skies of your game will now be filled with AI birds. The birds always start on the ground, and will only fly away in the presence of a predator.

New feature 2: Animal stat changes
Hares are now larger, to represent their real world scale compared to other animals. Hares also have increased health to go along with this.
Weasels were given stat changes to improve walking speed (it was unbearably slow before).

New feature 3: Stoat pounce
Stoats can now pounce onto Hares! Called the "Hug of Doom", Stoats now have the power to kill hares via a single successful pounce. Currently, it does not require stamina to use (this may change in the future).

New feature 4: Fall damage
All animals are now impacted by gravity. Basically, don't fall off of a cliff. Animals can still handle a jump every now and again, just don't jump to far...

Enjoy, and have a blessed day!

notes.title: DEV BLOG #3
notes.content:
This morning I worked on a simple flight system for AI birds! You heard right, AI birds are going to be added to the game eventually. They won't do anything fancy, but they will flap away from you at a decent pace.

This AI logic also can be applied to fish (strangely enough) to enable flight-like movement underwater.

How it works is a bit complex, so I'll spare the details and say that AI animals that fly and swim will be arriving sometime in the future with reasonable quality.

In other news, I've noticed that the game is getting loads of views and attention from the steam community. Thank you so much for giving my game traffic and I hope you will please consider trying the game. I plan on doing a sale with the next major update, so stay tuned!

Lately I have been taking a break from game development to refresh, relax, and come up with new ideas for future projects. If you have a question about my game or any questions regarding future titles, please post in the forums. I would love to hear your feedback!

Ty, and have a blessed weekend!

notes.title: DEV BLOG #2
notes.content:
Hello, Jacob here! This Sunday I'd like to talk to you about the next update to the game. Currently, I plan on adding a few new animals to existing maps to fill in gaps in the foodchain. I feel that the weasels are missing key food sources as the hares are too strong for juvenile weasels to tackle. I may introduce playable/AI voles and mice in the next few updates to address this problem.

Update 1.2 cannot be given a due date as of yet. I'm waiting to work on it as soon as the game's initial launch discount period is up. 

In other news, I'm going to host an event on the game's forums from June 6th to the 10th. In this forum event, you must either suggest a real world animal that lives in Europe that isn't currently in-game OR you can suggest a fictional animal that is similar to a European species. All suggestions are welcome, and suggested animals can be from modern times or from any time during the Holocene epoch (earth's current time frame and the time frame my game's world is set in). Extinct species are allowed to be suggested, but they must have existed during the Holocene.

notes.title: DEV BLOG #1
notes.content:
Hello, I am the Developer of Jacob Larkin's Wild Europe!

Here is a full breakdown of the game:
The game takes place in an alternate timeline of Europe, approximately 5,000 years ago. 
In this timeline there are no humans, and animals have full reign over the earth.

Gameplay-wise, you start out with the option to choose your character. Once chosen, you can roam about the map as your chosen species freely, with no need to worry about overly long and grindy
progression systems. Just hop in and have fun!

The first things I plan on adding into the game are new species and improvements to existing species. 
For instance, the Wild Boar will be getting some TLC in the new update 1.1.0 after the game releases on June 14th, so stay tuned! Furthermore, Content update 1.1.0 will include at least 4 new species of bird!

For those who don't know, the game is entirely friends-only multiplayer, meaning that you cannot join someone's game if you are not friended on Steam! The reasoning behind this is to prevent hacking players from interrupting the gameplay of those who just want to play the game. It also reduces the risk of toxic players from getting in the way of you and your friends.

The game isn't complete by any means, but I plan on updating it for as long as I see fit.
Take care, and have fun everyone!
